subtopic: Diversification Across and Within Asset Classes
source_evidence: You’ll also be better diversified if you spread your investments within each asset class.
answer: Diversification means spreading investments to reduce risk. You can diversify across asset classes by holding different kinds of assets, such as stocks and bonds. You can also diversify within an asset class—for example, by holding stocks from different companies or industry sectors. This way, if one asset, investment, or sector performs poorly, other holdings may help offset the loss. A fund is not necessarily diversified if it focuses narrowly on one sector.
